answer: Report: Which customers are in the top 10% by total spend, and what is their average order frequency?
sql:
WITH spend AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0) AS total_spend
    FROM ds_retail_customers c
    LEFT JOIN ds_retail_orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN ds_retail_payments p ON o.order_id = p.order_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        total_spend,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_spend DESC) AS pct_rank
    FROM spend
),
order_freq AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        COUNT(order_id) AS order_frequency
    FROM ds_retail_orders
    GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT
    AVG(COALESCE(of.order_frequency, 0)) AS avg_order_frequency_top10
FROM ranked r
LEFT JOIN order_freq of ON r.customer_id = of.customer_id
WHERE r.pct_rank <= 0.1;
question: Which customers are in the top 10% by total spend, and what is their average order frequency?

answer: Report: Compare Q4 vs Q3 revenue by region, identify the top 3 growth categories, and explain the driver behind the growth
sql:
WITH max_year AS (
    SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM MAX(order_date))::int AS yr FROM ds_retail_orders
)
SELECT
    p.category,
    CASE
        WHEN o.order_date >= make_date(my.yr, 7, 1)
             AND o.order_date <  make_date(my.yr, 10, 1) THEN 'Q3'
        WHEN o.order_date >= make_date(my.yr, 10, 1)
             AND o.order_date <  make_date(my.yr + 1, 1, 1) THEN 'Q4'
    END AS quarter,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.unit_price)::numeric, 2) AS avg_unit_price
FROM ds_retail_order_items oi
JOIN ds_retail_orders o    ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN ds_retail_products p  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
CROSS JOIN max_year my
WHERE o.order_date IS NOT NULL
  AND (
       (o.order_date >= make_date(my.yr, 7, 1)  AND o.order_date < make_date(my.yr, 10, 1))
    OR (o.order_date >= make_date(my.yr, 10, 1) AND o.order_date < make_date(my.yr + 1, 1, 1))
  )
GROUP BY p.category,
         CASE
            WHEN o.order_date >= make_date(my.yr, 7, 1)
                 AND o.order_date <  make_date(my.yr, 10, 1) THEN 'Q3'
            WHEN o.order_date >= make_date(my.yr, 10, 1)
                 AND o.order_date <  make_date(my.yr + 1, 1, 1) THEN 'Q4'
         END
ORDER BY p.category, quarter;
question: Compare Q4 vs Q3 revenue by region, identify the top 3 growth categories, and explain the driver behind the growth

answer: Report: Build a report on customer retention: what percentage of customers from Q1 2023 made a purchase in Q4 2023, broken down by segment, and which segment retained best?
sql:
SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS q1_customers
FROM ds_retail_orders o
JOIN ds_retail_customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.status = 'completed'
  AND o.order_date >= DATE '2023-01-01'
  AND o.order_date < DATE '2023-04-01'
GROUP BY c.segment;
